core.title: Give each acceptance a legacy id of the form AC-{STEP}-{NNN}
core.given: You are authoring or editing an acceptance and setting its legacy id (the backward-compatibility identifier kept alongside the acceptance URN, declared in the field named by the profile).
core.when: You write the legacy id value.
core.then: Write the legacy id as AC-{STEP}-{NNN}, where {STEP} is the step code mapped from the acceptance's step name by the step-code mapping (define→DEF, locate→LOC, prepare→PREP, confirm→CONF, execute→EXEC, monitor→MON, modify→MOD, resolve→RES, conclude→CONC) and {NNN} is the number.
prefer: Derive {STEP} strictly from the step-code mapping (step name → id code) rather than abbreviating the step name ad hoc.
Keep {NNN} as a three-digit number, as in the canonical examples of the reference realization.
avoid: Using full step names or non-mapped abbreviations in the id.
Treating the legacy AC id as a replacement for the acceptance URN; it is a parallel, backward-compatibility identifier.
core.why: The legacy AC id is kept for backward compatibility.
evidence: The declared legacy id of each acceptance matches AC-{STEP}-{NNN} with {STEP} one of DEF, LOC, PREP, CONF, EXEC, MON, MOD, RES, CONC.
{STEP} equals the step code mapped from the acceptance's step name.
verification: Mechanical pattern check over the declaration field supplied by the profile: every acceptance's legacy id must match AC-{STEP}-{NNN} with {STEP} one of the mapped step codes (define→DEF, locate→LOC, prepare→PREP, confirm→CONF, execute→EXEC, monitor→MON, modify→MOD, resolve→RES, conclude→CONC) and {NNN} a three-digit number; the exact pattern rendering (e.g. a regular expression) is realization mechanics.
Checking that {STEP} equals the step code mapped from the acceptance's step name requires reading the acceptance's step name; a pure shape check does not cover it.
The check governs only the legacy id; it does not cover the acceptance URN (governed by the URN-generation convention) and does not apply to artifacts that declare no acceptance identity.

values: acceptance legacy id added or modified

fires: Planner writes a new acceptance and must fill its legacy id
Planner renames or renumbers an acceptance's legacy id
Planner moves an acceptance to a different step and the step code in its id must change
doesNotFire: Editing only the acceptance URN (governed by the URN-generation convention)
Editing acceptance body text without touching the legacy id
Authoring other plan artifacts (wagons, WMBTs) or docs that contain no acceptance identity

profileRequirements.meaning: That 'acceptance' is one of the concrete plan-artifact kinds, so the rule can recognize which artifacts are acceptances (by kind/path).
The field or syntax by which an acceptance declares its legacy (backward-compatibility) id, so the obligation, activation and pattern check know which field to read and write.

proposedKeys.meaning: The field or syntax by which an acceptance declares its legacy (backward-compatibility) id, parallel to the acceptance URN.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: urn.acceptance and urn.binding.acceptance describe the acceptance URN and its binding, and urn.declaration describes a plan artifact's own URN; no key describes where the parallel legacy id is declared, which is artifact-schema data that varies by realization.

bunOnly.reason: Concrete canonical id examples are illustrative and stay in the Bun reference realization; the core states the pattern without them.

bunOnly.text: as in the canonical examples (AC-EXEC-201, AC-CONF-004)
bunOnly.reason: Concrete example ids are not repeated in the core; the three-digit width itself is kept in the core.
Concrete counter-examples stay in the Bun reference realization.
Reference examples for verifiers stay with the realization.
The regular-expression rendering and the concrete application target are realization mechanics; the core's verification states the same check generically and takes the field from the profile.

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely method-level: the AC-{STEP}-{NNN} shape, the step-code mapping (define→DEF … conclude→CONC) and the three-digit number width belong to the ATDD legacy corpus and name no stack, so they stay in the core rather than the profile. Only two things are realization data: the declaration field 'identity.id' (proposed key urn.legacy_id.acceptance, analogous to urn.declaration) and the recognition of acceptance artifacts (roles.plan_artifact.kinds). Concrete id examples and counter-examples, and the regular-expression rendering of the check, remain only in the Bun reference (bunOnly).
